description: Caller claims victim won lottery, sweepstakes, or prize but must pay fees or taxes first to claim winnings
indicators: claiming victim won lottery or sweepstakes
requesting payment for taxes or processing fees
mentioning Publishers Clearing House or other legitimate contests
requiring immediate action to claim prize
asking for personal information to verify identity
threatening prize expiration if not claimed quickly
example_scripts: Congratulations! You've won $1 million in the Publishers Clearing House sweepstakes. Pay $500 in taxes to claim your prize.
You're the lucky winner of our grand prize! Just send us $200 for processing fees.
We need your bank account number to deposit your $50,000 prize winnings.
You've been selected as the winner of our international lottery. Pay $1,000 in customs fees to receive your prize.
This is your final chance to claim your $100,000 prize. Send payment for taxes today or forfeit your winnings.
Congratulations! You won a new car. We just need your credit card to cover the registration fees.
You're one of three finalists for our million-dollar prize. Pay $300 to enter the final drawing.
Your name was randomly selected from our database. Claim your $25,000 prize by paying processing fees now.
You won the lottery! We need to verify your identity with your Social Security number and bank details.
Act now! Your prize expires in 24 hours. Send $500 via wire transfer to claim your $75,000 winnings.
red_flags: Legitimate lotteries don't require payment to claim prizes
You can't win a lottery you didn't enter
Real prizes don't require upfront fees
Legitimate organizations don't ask for gift cards
Winners are notified by certified mail, not phone
Real contests don't threaten prize expiration
Legitimate lotteries deduct taxes from winnings
